extracted.intended_audience: researchers (authors and reviewers) in the life and biomedical sciences; prospective eLife authors and editors
extracted.subtask_description: The journal-level policy describing eLife's peer review process for life and biomedical sciences, emphasizing faster, fairer, and more open review. It specifies the outputs of review, who makes decisions, constraints on revision requests, and transparency practices (e.g., publishing reviews alongside accepted manuscripts and preprints).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim to improve speed, visibility and usefulness of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife aims to improve the speed, visibility and usefulness of peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall aim articulated as making peer review faster, fairer and more open; envisions a future where outputs of peer review are the primary way research is assessed rather than journal title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review outputs: public reviews and detailed author feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Our editorial process produces two outputs: i) public reviews designed to be posted alongside a preprint for the benefit of the community; ii) detailed feedback on the manuscript for the authors, including requests for revisions and suggestions for improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public reviews are intended to be posted alongside preprints (publish-then-review model); detailed feedback should include revision recommendations and concrete suggestions for improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions made by active researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: All decisions are made by editors who are active researchers in the life and biomedical sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial decision-making is in the hands of practicing researchers to ensure expert assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: No artificial publication limits or set acceptance rate
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not artificially limit the number of articles we publish or have a set acceptance rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance is not governed by quotas or fixed acceptance percentages; quality and fit guide publication decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collegial discussion between editors and reviewers before decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors and reviewers discuss their reviews with each other before reaching a decision on a manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collective discussion among reviewers and editors precedes the decision to help reach a considered outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extra experiments requested only when essential and time-feasible (~two months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extra experiments are only requested if they are essential and can be reasonably completed within about two months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits the burden of revision on authors by requiring that additional work be both necessary to support claims and realistically doable in a short timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish reviews, revision recommendations, and author responses with accepted manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: The public reviews, revision recommendations, and author responses are published with accepted manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures transparency of the review process by making reviewer reports, requested revisions, and author replies publicly available alongside the final paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for publish-then-review / public posting alongside preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Public reviews are designed to be posted alongside a preprint for the benefit of the community; see 'Publish, then Review' model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages early dissemination (preprints) with open review appended publicly, shifting assessment to review outputs rather than journal prestige.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject reliance on journal Impact Factor; endorsement of DORA
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife does not support the Impact Factor and is a co-founder of the Declaration on Research Assessment (DORA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy stance discourages using journal-level metrics (Impact Factor) to assess research; aligns with DORA principles to evaluate research on its own merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularly updated editorial-process metrics available
rubrics_metrics.description: Regularly updated metrics relating to the eLife editorial process are available in our Author Guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eLife tracks and publishes metrics about its editorial process to provide transparency and allow monitoring of goals like speed and openness.
